name: Energy
summary: Energy platforms for monitoring, efficiency, and sustainability.
description: Energy UI UX design for grid, solar, EV charging and utility products: monitoring dashboards, usage analytics and customer apps that make energy data clear.
image_alt: Wind turbines at sunrise, energy industry
overview:
Energy products deal with a lot of data and a lot at stake. Operators watch assets and alarms around the clock, analysts look for patterns in usage, and customers just want to know what they are paying for. When the interface is noisy, important alerts get missed and good data goes unused.

I work with founders and product teams on web and mobile energy products, from early prototypes to a design system engineers can build from directly. My experience designing monitoring dashboards, such as Nimbus, where I redesigned how metrics surface priority and context to cut alert fatigue, shapes how I approach telemetry, alarms and reporting.

challenges.title: Alert fatigue
challenges.text: Operators see so many alarms that the critical ones get lost in the noise.

challenges.title: Complex telemetry
challenges.text: Readings from meters, inverters and sensors have to become something people can act on.

challenges.title: Energy literacy
challenges.text: Most customers do not think in kilowatt-hours, so usage and bills need plain explanations.

challenges.title: Credible reporting
challenges.text: Sustainability and emissions figures need clear sources and methods before people trust them.

faqs.question: Have you designed energy products before?
faqs.answer: My closest published work is Nimbus, a monitoring dashboard where I redesigned how metrics surface priority and context to cut alert fatigue. The same approach applies to asset monitoring and alarm handling, and I learn your domain in detail during discovery.

faqs.question: How do you handle large amounts of telemetry data?
faqs.answer: I start from the decisions people need to make, then choose the summaries, charts and drill-downs that support them. Raw data stays available, but it is not the first thing people see.

faqs.question: Can you design for both operators and consumers?
faqs.answer: Yes. I can design a detailed console for operations teams and a simple app for customers, built on one shared design system.

faqs.question: Do you design for both web and mobile?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most energy products need a web dashboard and a mobile app for customers or field engineers, so I design both on one system.

faqs.question: How do we start?
faqs.answer: Send me a short brief through the contact page. We will have a call about your product, users and timeline, and I will come back with a plan and quote.
